question: How many confirmed measles cases will Peru's CDC-MINSA report nationally for 2026 as of mid-October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Last confirmed CDC-MINSA national figure: 2,543 (~Oct 1); PAHO 2,553 through ~Oct 3. Reported cumulative growth averaged ~136/wk Aug 21-Oct 1 (1,747->2,543), with 150-190/wk in late September due to reclassification, while onset-date curve peaked ~SE35 and is declining (lag-affected). Two more weeks of reported growth to an Oct 15 cut at 100-190/wk gives ~2,740-2,920; median ~2,790. Lower tail covers decline/stale-cut use; upper tail covers reclassification bursts or Lima/Amazon spread. No human market found (Kalshi/Polymarket only US measles).
sources: WebSearch results: abc.com.py 2026-09-24 (2,357), PAHO 2,553 report, Kalshi measles market listings
calls.dossier:
- CDC-MINSA Sala Situacional figure reported ~2026-10-01: 2,543 confirmed 2026 cases (ATV, Infobae, La Republica 2026-10-01). National incidence 7.34/100k; Puno 120.63, Madre de Dios 86.91, Arequipa 10.03, Loreto 9.64, Ucayali 4.09.
- PAHO regional update (Jan 4-Oct 3 2026, published ~Oct 9): Peru 2,553 confirmed, 1 death (search snippet).
- Alert dated 2026-09-26 (Global Risk Atlas, pub Oct 1): 2,438 confirmed, first death, community transmission in Loreto.
- 2026-09-24 (ABC Color/EFE): 2,357 confirmed plus a death of a 16-year-old in Loreto.
- Mid-Sept: ~1,929 confirmed (question background). SE33 (~Aug 21) alert AE-CDC-007-2026: 1,747 (Puno 1,264). July 26-28: 1,233-1,236. SE22 (Jun 4): 501. May 21: >300.
- Implied reported cumulative increments: Aug 21->Oct 1 ~+796 over ~6 weeks (~136/wk); Sep 24->Oct 1 ~+186; Sep 26->Oct 1 ~+105.
- Onset-date curve (CDC-MINSA chart via Infobae/ATV): >100/wk from SE20, peak ~150 around SE35; latest bars lower but flagged as subject to upward revision (reporting lag).
- Ex-vice minister Percy Minaya (Infobae 2026-09-26) warned cases could quadruple; vaccine coverage drops cited; Amazon Indigenous areas ~50% coverage; 29 cases in Lima Este (Sep 30).
- 90-day health emergency declared May 2026; alerts in 24 departments.
- Status quo: cumulative count keeps rising each week; it cannot fall unless reclassified.
- Resolution: resolves off the CDC-MINSA national confirmed total for the latest data cut dated on or before 2026-10-15 (or credible media citing CDC-MINSA), not PAHO's regional tables or suspected cases.
- Event window: cumulative from 2026-01-01 -> data cut <= 2026-10-15; as of 2026-10-12 ~2 weeks of growth since the last public figure (Oct 1) remain to be counted.
- Searched but not found: any national figure published after Oct 1 2026; exact data-cut dates/epi weeks behind 2,543; human prediction markets on Peru's count (none found).
calls.reference_class: Recent reported weekly cumulative increments in Peru's 2026 measles outbreak (Aug-Oct 2026), extrapolated over the remaining ~2-week horizon

Cases by onset peaked ~SE35 and are falling, but ~6,100 suspected cases leave a reclassification backlog. Roughly two more weeks of reporting to an Oct 15 cut at ~100-170/wk gives a median near 2,785. The low tail covers a stale dashboard, the high tail a burst of reclassifications. calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the anchor (2,543 at ~Oct 1; PAHO 2,553 to Oct 3) and on the recent reporting pace (~136/wk average, ~186/wk late Sept), with onset-date cases falling after a ~SE35 peak. One factual dispute could not be settled without web access: whether the dashboard updated after Oct 1 (an Oct 11 ATV article still cites 2,543), so it stays in the low tail. Since resolution waits for the latest cut dated on or before Oct 15, a stale dashboard mostly widens the low tail rather than moving the median. Weighing a slowing onset curve against the suspected-case backlog is judgment; I bet on ~100-170/wk for about two weeks, a median ~2,785. I carried forward the runs' shared reference class, with dispersion ~390, which sits inside their 360-420.
